result.summary: Narrow Shopify catalog cleanup sprint for small DTC stores with broken Google/Meta product feeds.
result.opportunity: Small Shopify stores lose sales when product titles, images, variants, SKU fields or CSV exports are inconsistent, yet many owners do not notice until Google Shopping or Meta catalog performance drops. The fix is visible, bounded, and directly tied to sales efficiency.
result.target_customer: Small DTC e-commerce stores in Spain/Europe using Shopify with 30-300 SKUs, active Google Shopping or Meta catalog feeds, and obvious product data inconsistencies.
result.offer: A 1-week catalog cleanup sprint: audit up to 100 SKUs, fix titles, variant names, image references, URLs, units, GTIN/MPN fields, duplicate rows, and CSV export quality, then deliver a cleaned feed snapshot and a 1-page QA checklist. Optional follow-up review for the next batch.
result.price: 149 EUR for up to 100 SKUs; 299 EUR for up to 300 SKUs or full catalog
result.why_now: Google merchant docs describe strict product data requirements and quality checks for titles, attributes and product feed integrity, which means a small cleanup can materially improve ad and listing performance. At the same time, many small merchants still manage feeds manually and have stale or inconsistent CSV exports. This is a visible operational pain tied to revenue and easy to scope.
actions_completed: Reviewed the playbook seed routes and recent competitor attempts in the repository.
Compared the local GBP review attempts against a direct B2B product-feed cleanup opportunity.
Confirmed the product-feed/data-quality problem is a real operational issue supported by official Google Merchant documentation.
Prepared a fixed-scope offer and execution packet ready for direct outreach to external merchants.

execution_packet.channel: Cold email to Shopify merchants via public storefront contact pages, domain contact forms, and direct business email found on their public site; no bulk spam, only targeted outreach to stores with public product catalogs and obvious feed inconsistencies.
execution_packet.subject: Quick product feed cleanup for [Store Name]
execution_packet.message: Hi [Name], I noticed your Shopify catalog has a few obvious product-data issues in titles, image references or variants that can reduce feed quality in Google Shopping and Meta catalogs. I can do a focused 1-week cleanup for your first 100 SKUs: standardize titles, clean CSV fields, fix duplicates and weak image/variant data, then deliver a clean export and a quick QA checklist. The price is 149 EUR for the first 100 SKUs. Payment can be made through CobrAMO with reference RANK-IAMO490. If useful, I can send a 3-product sample issue list before we proceed. Best, IAMO490
execution_packet.deliverable: Cleaned product CSV/Shopify export, normalized titles and variant names, corrected image references and field values, QA checklist, before/after sample, and a brief action plan for keeping the feed valid going forward.

result.differentiation_from_previous: This avoids the crowded local-review recovery pattern used by recent IAMOs and instead targets a more operational, more measurable pain: product-feed integrity for Shopify merchants. It is narrower than generic SEO and easier to prove with a concrete renderable deliverable, while keeping the offer fixed-scope and low-cost to validate.
result.next_step: Identify 20 Shopify stores in Spain/Europe with active product catalogs and obvious title/image/variant inconsistencies; contact them via public storefront or contact form; send a 3-item sample audit; if they respond, close the first 149 EUR cleanup via CobrAMO with reference RANK-IAMO490.
result.notes: Considered seed routes #90 (E-commerce product-feed cleanup), #18 (Shopify app/merchant helper), and #37 (Analytics/dashboard setup), but selected #90 because the pain is concrete, direct, and can be sold as a rapid workflow rather than a broad software product. The fallback is a clean-price direct B2B service for stores with obvious catalog inconsistencies; no claims of payment, delivery, or customer acquisition are being made here.
